content.value_statement: Teams need chat interfaces that feel consistent with modern React applications. This skill provides reusable chat component patterns for React, Next.js, and shadcn-style projects.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to add chat components from the ui.inference.sh registry.
Provides React examples for chat containers, messages, inputs, and typing indicators.
Demonstrates message roles for user, assistant, and system messages.
Includes a full chat component example with local message state.
Links to related documentation for agent chat, UX patterns, and streaming responses.
limitations: Does not include backend API implementation for message delivery.
Requires a React or Next.js project with compatible styling setup.
Uses external install commands that users should review before running.
Does not provide authentication, persistence, moderation, or rate limiting.

use_cases.title: Prototype an AI Assistant
use_cases.description: Create a chat screen with message bubbles, input handling, and loading feedback for early product testing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Chat Components
use_cases.description: Use shared React examples to keep message layouts and interaction states consistent across an application.

use_cases.title: Plan Streaming Chat UX
use_cases.description: Combine typing indicators and linked guidance to design responsive agent conversations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chat View
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chat-ui skill to build a simple React chat view with messages, an input, and a typing indicator.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small chat interface.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Components to My Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my React project structure and show where the chat container, message, and input components should be placed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Integrating the examples into an existing application.

prompt_templates.title: Design Loading and Empty States
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend the chat UI pattern with empty, loading, disabled, and error states that match my current design system.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving user experience around conversation states.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Streaming Assistant Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chat-ui examples to design a streaming assistant interface with message roles, pending responses, and accessible controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation for AI assistant workflows.

output_examples.input: Create a basic support chat screen for a Next.js app.
output_examples.output: A React chat layout with a message container, user and assistant messages, a disabled state during loading, and a send input.

output_examples.input: Add feedback for an assistant response that is still generating.
output_examples.output: A chat flow that shows the latest user message, displays a typing indicator, and prevents duplicate sends while loading.

output_examples.input: Explain how to style assistant messages differently.
output_examples.output: Guidance for applying project design tokens to assistant message backgrounds while preserving role-based alignment.

best_practices: Review remote registry content before running install commands.
Keep chat state, loading state, and input disabled state synchronized.
Use clear role handling for user, assistant, and system messages.
anti_patterns: Do not run remote install commands without reviewing the fetched files.
Do not mix backend API logic into presentational chat components.
Do not hide loading or disabled states during message submission.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build React and Next.js chat interfaces with reusable component patterns.

faq.question: Does it include a backend chat service?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on frontend components and leaves API integration to your application.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support streaming responses?
faq.answer: It includes UI patterns and documentation links that help design streaming chat experiences.

faq.question: Are the install commands safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: They fetch external content, so users should inspect sources and pin trusted versions first.

faq.question: What projects are a good fit?
faq.answer: It fits React or Next.js projects that use Tailwind CSS and shadcn-style components.
